root_idea.summary: The root centers on causing fear or apprehension, especially by communicating a danger, and on becoming wary of a danger.
root_idea.development: From warning and taking heed developed the sense of informing someone with an admonitory or threatening implication. The noun نَذْر also denotes an obligation voluntarily imposed on oneself, as though one fears the consequence of failing to fulfill it.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form نَذَرَ.
Displayed under the normalized Form IV perfect citation form أَنْذَرَ.
Displayed under the singular passive-participle citation form مُنْذَر.
Displayed under the active-participle citation form مُنْذِر.
Displayed as the lexical noun نَذِير, including its Quranic plural surface forms نُذُر.
Displayed as the warning noun نُذْر.
نُذُور is the supplied plural of نَذْر and is normalized under the singular vow citation form.
Displayed under the normalized singular noun نَذْر; the merged form also contains its plural نُذُور.

senses.definition: To vow; make an act, offering, or future action binding or obligatory upon oneself.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with the person making the vow as subject, often with عَلَى نَفْسِهِ or لِلّٰهِ. The Quranic use includes voluntarily dedicating a child to religious service by vow.

senses.definition: To become aware of something and take heed of it; become wary or remain on guard against it.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic passive occurrence presents the result as being warned or made aware and cautious of a danger.

senses.definition: To warn someone of a danger or consequence; caution, put on guard, or put in fear by communicating it.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is used for announcing punishment, danger, or an impending event in an admonitory context. Voice, tense, and object marking vary grammatically without changing the lexical sense.

senses.definition: One who has been warned, cautioned, or put in fear.
senses.usage_conditions: This is the passive-participial state resulting from being warned or admonished; the Quran uses the plural form for those who have received such warning.

senses.definition: One who warns or cautions; a warner.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran uses the active participle for individual or collective bearers of warning, including prophetic warners.

senses.definition: A warner; one who gives notice of a danger, enemy, or other consequential matter.
senses.usage_conditions: The term may denote a human or a nonhuman bearer of warning. Its plural نُذُر occurs in Quranic contexts referring either to warners or to warnings, according to construction and interpretation.

senses.definition: A warning, admonition, or warning-sign; something that conveys notice of danger or consequence.
senses.usage_conditions: This substantival use is especially visible where نَذِير refers to the warning itself rather than exclusively to its bearer.

senses.definition: A messenger or prophet in the role of a bearer of warning.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quran-focused interpretive use identifies النَّذِير with the apostle or Prophet as the bearer of warning. The historical citation attached to this interpretation is not converted here into a modern verse location.

senses.definition: Hoariness or whiteness of the hair.
senses.usage_conditions: This is a less probable alternative interpretation reported for a Quranic expression in the lexical discussion, rather than the ordinary Quranic sense of نَذِير.

senses.definition: A warning or admonition, especially one intended to put someone on guard or in fear.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction عُذْرًا أَوْ نُذْرًا, the noun functions as a causal complement meaning warning or admonition.

senses.definition: A vow: a voluntary undertaking by which a person makes an act, offering, or payment binding upon oneself, either absolutely or conditionally.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form includes both singular نَذْر and plural نُذُور. A conditional vow may make an undertaking obligatory upon the occurrence of a specified event.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To inform or advise someone of a matter, without the warning or frightening implication that often accompanies the verb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical Arabic use distinguished from the Quran-attested admonitory use; the information may concern a matter or the movement of an enemy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To warn or caution one another, or put one another in fear of a terrifying danger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used reciprocally of a group mutually warning each other about a feared matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To offer or give warning to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical Form X construction with the person warned expressed by إِلَى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Compensation or a mulct owed for an intentional wound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical and dialectal usage, equated with أَرْش; it is distinct from the vow meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A votive offering made in fulfillment of a vow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical nominal specialization of the vow branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A scout or spy who reports the presence or condition of an enemy to a people or army.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized human role within the broader branch of giving warning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing vowed or made the object of a vow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical use equating نَذِير with مَنْذُور, distinct from the ordinary sense of a warner.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Abū Mundhir, a traditional name or epithet for the cock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic naming usage, not a general meaning of every occurrence of نَذِير.
A figurative or lexicalized Classical usage explained by the warning or frightening effect of the sound on its target.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A votive gift or offering given by one who has made a vow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine noun denotes the offered object rather than the act of vowing itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A child vowed and appointed for service in a church or other place devoted to religious exercises.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized religious and social usage of the feminine noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who looks hard or intently, making the eye prominent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic expression describing an intense fixed gaze.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing of which people warn one another or which they cause one another to fear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a disease or other dreaded matter; the mutual-warning relation is part of the lexical meaning.
A figurative or tropical application of the term to a creature regarded as one of which people warn and frighten one another.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Vow and self-imposed obligation, including dedication by vow, are covered.
Awareness, caution, and being on guard are covered.
The warning and broader informing branches are both represented.
Reciprocal warning and frightening are represented.
The vow and its plural are covered by the Quranic vow sense.
The wound mulct specialization is represented.
Warning, admonition, and putting in fear are represented for the two Quranic nominal realizations.
The general warner and specialized enemy-reporter branches are represented.
The Quran-focused messenger or prophetic-warner interpretation is represented.
The less probable Quran-focused hoariness interpretation is retained.
The idiomatic intense-gaze meaning is represented.
A thing mutually warned against or feared is represented.
The tropical lion application is represented.

cautions: The reported interpretation of نَذِير as hoariness or whiteness of hair is retained as a less probable Quran-specific reading; the historical citation is not treated as a modern verse reference.
The Form I and Form IV passive imperfects can have the same visible Quranic surface pattern in transcription; the grouping and occurrence assignments follow the supplied QAC morphology.
